newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - JITTERY U.S. STOCKS FLASH BEAR SIGNALS.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JITTERY U.S. STOCKS FLASH BEAR SIGNALS.

text.p: The sharp gyrations by U.S. stocks on Wednesday could be a sign that the market may be headed for further near-term losses, technical analysts said.
Heightened sensitivity to news coupled with sharp price swings after an extended rally can indicate near-term pullbacks lie ahead.
"That's the kind of action you've got right here," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Early on Wednesday, the Dow jumped 80 points, reacting to benign data on U.S. July retail sales and wholesale inflation.

But a reversal in the bond market slammed the brakes on the rally, sending the Dow skidding to a session low, down 82 points. By afternoon dealings, the blue chip guage recovered and was up 15 points at 7975.
Harrington said the sharp reversal, coupled other recent bearish signs such as a relatively low put/call ratio, had him expecting a further correction.
"It would appear there's a very good chance of the market moving into the mid-7,000s (on the Dow) over the next few days or next few weeks," Harrington said.
Other analysts said Wednesday's action was not enough to draw solid conclusions on the market's near-term direction.
Jonathan Dodd, technical analyst at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, said the Dow was still well above a key near-term support level at 7800-7850.
The drive from the market's April lows has been marked by short, sharp pullbacks that did not short ciruit the rally. If that pattern holds, most of the current downturn could be over, Dodd said.
The Dow rallied 29 percent from its 1997 closing low on April 11 at 6391.69 to its record closing high August 6 at 8259.31.
Dodd said a key signal will be the market's performance in any fresh rallies.

"If it can get back to the highs again, and there's no reason to think that it can't at this point, then it will be fine," he said. "If it fails to make new highs after this pullback, then it's in a weakening position," he said.
Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities, said the latest market moves were making him "very nervous."
He said was was watching the action of software giant Microsoft Corp as a bellwether for both technology shares and the overall market.
Microsoft's ability to hold near-term support at the 134 level could be an important test for the market as a whole, he said.
If that level were to break "that would be a sign we might be in for a five-to-10 percent correction such as we had in March and April," Tower said.
Microsoft was up 3/8 at 136-3/8 in afternoon trading after touching 134-3/4 earlier in the session.
